newsitem.title: CHINA: China needs bank, broker barriers -- central bank.
newsitem.headline: China needs bank, broker barriers -- central bank.

text.p: China needs to limit financial sector risk and cannot afford to allow an overlap of securities and banking business in the near future, a top central banker said on Wednesday.
"It is too early," vice governor Chen Yuan told Reuters in reply to a question as to whether barriers could be removed anytime soon.
"We still need a period of time."
China has been trying to limit risk in its financial markets and part of the drive has focused on keeping the two sectors separate.
Beijing has warned banks against using funds to finance stock purchases and has forced them to divest their trust company subsidiaries, which are permitted to pump money into equities trading.
It has also barred securities houses from conducting banking operations.
China was stunned by the collapse of one of its biggest trust companies, the China Agribusiness Trust and Investment Corp, earlier this year.
Chen blamed the company's losses on high risk real estate investments.
Chen, speaking after an international securities conference, acknowledged that many developed countries were moving in the opposite direction, breaking down barriers within financial markets.
He told the conference that as China moved to dismantle its centrally planned economy and replace it with market-style principles, risks to the nation's financial system were relatively large.
"In the monitoring of the securities market, one of our fundamental policies is to strengthen management by industry separation and controlling financial risk," Chen said.

This means the "strict prohibition of participation by non-banking financial institutions including securities houses from conducting banking operations and prohibition of banks from engaging in securities trading", he said.
